title: Chapter 1 Subpart A - Nature and Regulation of Companies
description: A challenging assessment of company characteristics, classifications, formation, administration, funding, corporate regulation, accounting standard setting and financial reporting requirements.
subject: ACC2372 - Advanced Financial Accounting and Reporting

questions.question: The directors of a registered company enter into a transaction that is outside the objectives stated in its constitution. Which conclusion best reflects the legal capacity of the company?
options: The transaction is automatically invalid because constitutional objectives strictly limit corporate capacity
The transaction remains within the company's legal capacity even though it may conflict with its stated objectives
The transaction becomes valid only if every shareholder subsequently approves the directors' decision
The transaction is valid only when the counterparty was unaware of the objectives stated in the constitution
questions.answer: The transaction remains within the company's legal capacity even though it may conflict with its stated objectives
questions.rationale: A registered company has broad legal capacity and an act is not invalid merely because it is contrary to objectives stated in its constitution.

questions.question: A shareholder has fully paid for all shares held in a company limited by shares. The company later becomes insolvent with substantial unpaid debts. Which outcome most directly follows from limited liability?
options: The shareholder must contribute proportionately to all remaining company debts
The shareholder becomes jointly liable with directors for outstanding creditor claims
The shareholder is generally not required to contribute further amounts in respect of those fully paid shares
The shareholder must surrender personal assets whenever company assets are insufficient
questions.answer: The shareholder is generally not required to contribute further amounts in respect of those fully paid shares
questions.rationale: Liability of a member in a company limited by shares is generally limited to amounts unpaid on the member's shares.

questions.question: Which event best demonstrates the principle of perpetual succession arising from separate legal existence?
options: A shareholder sells shares and the company continues to hold the same assets and obligations
A director resigns and all contracts entered into during that director's term automatically terminate
A shareholder dies and the company must immediately be registered as a new legal entity
A company changes its business strategy and therefore receives a new corporate identity
questions.answer: A shareholder sells shares and the company continues to hold the same assets and obligations
questions.rationale: Changes in membership do not terminate the separate legal existence of a company, which continues until deregistration.

questions.question: A company changes its registered name after several years of operation. Which statement best describes the effect of this change?
options: Its existing obligations end because the previous legal identity no longer exists
Its ACN changes while its contractual obligations remain attached to the previous number
Its legal rights transfer to a newly incorporated entity bearing the new company name
Its ACN and existing rights and obligations remain unaffected by the change of name
questions.answer: Its ACN and existing rights and obligations remain unaffected by the change of name
questions.rationale: The ACN remains with the company throughout its life and a change of name does not alter its existing rights or obligations.

questions.question: Which proposed structure is inconsistent with the characteristics of a proprietary company described in the Corporations Act?
options: A company limited by shares with one shareholder who is also its sole director
An unlimited company with share capital and a relatively small number of shareholders
A company limited by guarantee with one Australian resident director and no share capital
A company with share capital that does not undertake public fundraising requiring a disclosure document
questions.answer: A company limited by guarantee with one Australian resident director and no share capital
questions.rationale: A proprietary company must have share capital and cannot be registered as a company limited by guarantee.

questions.question: A proprietary company has 48 ordinary shareholders and 7 employee shareholders. Assuming all other requirements are satisfied, which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: It must convert to a public company because every shareholder counts toward the maximum of 50
It may remain proprietary because employee shareholders are excluded when applying the 50 shareholder limit
It must remove at least five shareholders because proprietary companies may have no more than 50 members of any kind
It may remain proprietary only if all employee shareholders surrender their voting rights
questions.answer: It may remain proprietary because employee shareholders are excluded when applying the 50 shareholder limit
questions.rationale: The maximum of 50 shareholders for a proprietary company excludes employee shareholders.

questions.question: A proprietary company satisfies only one of the three statutory tests for classification as a small proprietary company. How should it generally be classified?
options: Small because satisfying any one threshold is sufficient
Small if its directors voluntarily adopt reduced reporting requirements
Large because at least two of the specified tests must be satisfied to qualify as small
Large only if ASIC separately determines that public accountability exists
questions.answer: Large because at least two of the specified tests must be satisfied to qualify as small
questions.rationale: Under the chapter's thresholds, a proprietary company must satisfy at least two of the three tests to qualify as small.

questions.question: Which feature most clearly distinguishes the fundraising position of a public company from that of a proprietary company?
options: A public company can raise funds only through secured bank borrowing
A public company may invite public investment through an appropriate disclosure document
A proprietary company may issue securities publicly provided it has fewer than 50 shareholders
A proprietary company may issue debentures publicly but cannot issue shares publicly
questions.answer: A public company may invite public investment through an appropriate disclosure document
questions.rationale: Public companies may generally raise funds from the public subject to disclosure requirements, while proprietary companies face restrictions on public fundraising.

questions.question: An entity has issued securities that bring it within the enhanced disclosure regime. Which additional reporting consequence is most consistent with its status as a disclosing entity?
options: It is exempt from annual reporting because continuous disclosure replaces periodic reporting
It must prepare only special purpose financial reports for its security holders
It is subject to half yearly reporting and continuous disclosure requirements in addition to annual reporting
It is required to report only when ASIC specifically requests financial information
questions.answer: It is subject to half yearly reporting and continuous disclosure requirements in addition to annual reporting
questions.rationale: Disclosing entities face enhanced obligations including half yearly financial reporting and continuous disclosure.

questions.question: A foreign company incorporated outside Australia wishes to carry on business in Australia. Which combination most accurately reflects the requirements discussed in the chapter?
options: Register with ASIC and appoint at least one local agent
Register directly with the ASX and appoint three Australian directors
Obtain an ACN and convert automatically into an Australian proprietary company
Lodge a prospectus with the AASB and appoint an Australian auditor
questions.answer: Register with ASIC and appoint at least one local agent
questions.rationale: A foreign company carrying on business in Australia must generally register with ASIC and appoint at least one local agent.

questions.question: Which proposed company is most likely to qualify for registration as a no liability company?
options: A public mining company with share capital whose constitution prevents recovery of unpaid calls from defaulting shareholders
A proprietary exploration company that guarantees repayment of all unpaid calls
A public construction company without share capital that undertakes quarrying for road building
A company limited by guarantee whose principal activity is mineral exploration
questions.answer: A public mining company with share capital whose constitution prevents recovery of unpaid calls from defaulting shareholders
questions.rationale: A no liability company must have share capital, have mining purposes as its sole objects and lack a contractual right to recover unpaid calls.

questions.question: What is the strongest legal significance of the certificate of registration issued by ASIC?
options: It establishes that the company has obtained permission to list its securities
It proves that shareholders have fully paid all shares issued at registration
It provides conclusive evidence that registration requirements have been complied with and the company is duly registered
It confirms that ASIC guarantees the company's future compliance with the Corporations Act
questions.answer: It provides conclusive evidence that registration requirements have been complied with and the company is duly registered
questions.rationale: The certificate provides conclusive evidence of compliance with registration requirements and marks the company's legal existence from the specified registration date.

questions.question: A company wants internal governance arrangements different from the statutory replaceable rules. What is the most appropriate mechanism?
options: Apply to ASIC for permanent exemption from internal governance requirements
Adopt a constitution containing the alternative or additional internal rules
Replace the Corporations Act rules through an ordinary directors' resolution
Issue a disclosure document describing the proposed governance arrangements
questions.answer: Adopt a constitution containing the alternative or additional internal rules
questions.rationale: A company wishing to adopt different or additional internal rules may establish its own constitution.

questions.question: Which relationship is directly given contractual effect by a company's constitution and applicable replaceable rules?
options: The company and every external supplier regardless of contractual dealings
The company and each member, as well as specified internal relationships involving members and officers
The company and all future investors before they acquire any membership interest
The directors and government regulators independently of their statutory obligations
questions.answer: The company and each member, as well as specified internal relationships involving members and officers
questions.rationale: The constitution and applicable replaceable rules operate as a statutory contract among the company, members and specified company officers.

questions.question: A company modifies its constitution after a person becomes a member and the amendment requires that member to purchase additional shares. The member has not agreed in writing. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The member is automatically bound because every constitutional amendment applies retrospectively
The member is generally not bound by that modification without written agreement
The member is bound only if the company is a proprietary company
The member is automatically bound if directors unanimously approved the modification
questions.answer: The member is generally not bound by that modification without written agreement
questions.rationale: A member is generally not bound without written agreement by a later constitutional modification requiring the member to take up additional shares.

questions.question: Which record would provide the most direct evidence of the amount paid on shares and whether those shares are fully paid?
options: Register of option holders
Minute book of directors' meetings
Register of members
Register of debenture holders
questions.answer: Register of members
questions.rationale: Where a company has share capital, the register of members contains details including shares held, amounts paid and whether the shares are fully paid.

questions.question: An investor wants a financing instrument that normally establishes a creditor relationship rather than an ownership interest. Which security most closely satisfies this objective?
options: Ordinary share
Preference share
Debenture
Share option
questions.answer: Debenture
questions.rationale: A debenture represents borrowing by the company and generally creates a creditor relationship, unlike shares which represent ownership interests.

questions.question: Why are disclosure documents particularly important when companies seek funds from the public?
options: They eliminate all investment risk by guaranteeing the accuracy of future forecasts
They provide prospective investors with relevant information for evaluating the securities being offered
They transfer responsibility for investment decisions from investors to ASIC
They allow companies to avoid ongoing financial reporting after securities are issued
questions.answer: They provide prospective investors with relevant information for evaluating the securities being offered
questions.rationale: Disclosure requirements reduce information asymmetry by providing potential investors with information relevant to informed investment decisions.

questions.question: Which development most directly created the historical demand for greater accounting regulation and standardisation?
options: The separation of ownership from control and the resulting dependence of owners and external users on management reporting
The elimination of external investors from the financing of industrial organisations
The replacement of professional judgement with government ownership of companies
The reduction in organisational complexity following the growth of industrialised economies
questions.answer: The separation of ownership from control and the resulting dependence of owners and external users on management reporting
questions.rationale: The separation of ownership and control created stewardship and information problems that increased the need for reliable disclosure and accounting standards.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes the roles of the Financial Reporting Council and the Australian Accounting Standards Board?
options: The FRC develops individual accounting standards while the AASB enforces them against listed companies
The FRC provides strategic oversight while the AASB develops and formulates accounting standards
The AASB determines securities listing requirements while the FRC administers the Corporations Act
The FRC audits financial statements while the AASB supervises securities trading
questions.answer: The FRC provides strategic oversight while the AASB develops and formulates accounting standards
questions.rationale: The FRC oversees and provides broad strategic direction to the standard setting process, while the AASB performs the technical standard setting functions.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately explains the relationship between Australian and international accounting standards described in the chapter?
options: Australia develops standards independently and prohibits the adoption of international standards
The IASB directly enacts Australian accounting standards without involvement from Australian institutions
The AASB incorporates international standards into the Australian framework while accounting for relevant Australian requirements
The ASX replaces all IASB standards with its own Listing Rules for Australian companies
questions.answer: The AASB incorporates international standards into the Australian framework while accounting for relevant Australian requirements
questions.rationale: Australian standard setting is strongly influenced by IASB standards, which are adopted through the AASB and may include Australian specific requirements.

questions.question: A financial report is designed for external users who cannot demand reports tailored specifically to their individual information needs. How should the report most appropriately be classified?
options: A special purpose financial report
A management information report
A general purpose financial report
A regulatory investigation report
questions.answer: A general purpose financial report
questions.rationale: General purpose financial reports are intended to satisfy common information needs of users who cannot command individually tailored reports.

questions.question: Which circumstance provides the strongest indication that an entity is a reporting entity under the concept discussed in the chapter?
options: Management can identify no external users who depend on the entity's financial reports
Users exist who reasonably rely on general purpose financial reports when making and evaluating economic decisions
Every shareholder has direct access to all internal accounting records and can demand customised information
The entity prepares reports solely for internal budgeting and operational control
questions.answer: Users exist who reasonably rely on general purpose financial reports when making and evaluating economic decisions
questions.rationale: The reporting entity concept focuses on whether users are reasonably expected to depend on general purpose financial reports for economic decision making.

questions.question: A company comes into legal existence upon [dropdown_1], while its continuing legal identity despite changes in membership reflects [dropdown_2].

options: registration by ASIC
adoption of a constitution
first public share issue
appointment of an auditor
perpetual succession
public accountability
continuous disclosure
differential reporting

questions.rationale: Registration creates the company as a separate legal entity, while perpetual succession allows that entity to continue despite changes affecting individual members.

questions.question: In Australian accounting standard setting, the [dropdown_1] provides broad strategic oversight, while the [dropdown_2] develops and formulates accounting standards.

options: FRC
ASIC
ASX
IASB
AASB
ASIC
ASX
FRC

questions.rationale: The FRC oversees the standard setting process and determines broad strategic directions, while the AASB performs the accounting standard setting function.

questions.question: Under the differential reporting framework described in the chapter, publicly accountable entities generally apply [dropdown_1], while eligible entities applying Tier 2 retain full recognition and measurement requirements but receive [dropdown_2].

options: Tier 1 requirements
special purpose reporting only
no accounting standards
internal reporting requirements
reduced disclosures
reduced recognition rules
exemption from measurement rules
exemption from financial statements

questions.rationale: Tier 1 applies full requirements, while the Tier 2 approach described in the chapter retains recognition and measurement requirements with reduced disclosures.

questions.question: The unique number allocated to an Australian company on registration and retained throughout its life is the ________.
questions.answer: ACN
questions.rationale: ASIC allocates an Australian company number on registration and the number remains with the company even if its name changes.

questions.question: The statutory internal governance provisions that a company may use instead of creating all of its own constitutional rules are called ________ rules.
questions.answer: replaceable
questions.rationale: Replaceable rules contained in the Corporations Act can govern specified aspects of a company's internal affairs.

questions.question: An entity for which users are reasonably expected to rely on general purpose financial reports for economic decision making is known as a ________ entity.
questions.answer: reporting
questions.rationale: The reporting entity concept identifies entities whose users depend on general purpose financial reports for making and evaluating economic decisions.

questions.question: Which three characteristics arise directly from the separate legal existence of a company?
options: The company may own property in its own name
The company may enter contracts independently of its members
The company may sue and be sued
Every shareholder becomes personally liable for all company debts
The company automatically ceases when a controlling shareholder dies
answer: The company may own property in its own name
The company may enter contracts independently of its members
The company may sue and be sued
questions.rationale: Separate legal personality allows the company itself to own assets, assume contractual rights and obligations and participate in legal proceedings.

questions.question: Which three statements correctly describe important characteristics of a public company compared with a proprietary company?
options: It may be limited by guarantee
It generally has greater ability to raise funds from the public
It must have at least three directors, with at least two ordinarily resident in Australia
It can never have share capital
It is prohibited from appointing a company secretary
answer: It may be limited by guarantee
It generally has greater ability to raise funds from the public
It must have at least three directors, with at least two ordinarily resident in Australia
questions.rationale: Public companies may take forms unavailable to proprietary companies, can generally undertake public fundraising and are subject to greater governance requirements.

questions.question: Which three activities are consistent with the functions or objectives of the Australian accounting standard setting framework?
options: Developing accounting standards that support useful economic decision making
Promoting comparability and understandable financial information
Contributing to the development of globally consistent accounting standards
Guaranteeing that every entity will earn profits after adopting accounting standards
Preventing all entities from using professional judgement in financial reporting
answer: Developing accounting standards that support useful economic decision making
Promoting comparability and understandable financial information
Contributing to the development of globally consistent accounting standards
questions.rationale: The Australian standard setting framework seeks decision useful, comparable and understandable information while participating in international standard development.

questions.question: Match each company related concept with the situation that best illustrates it.

matchPairs.right: A fully paid shareholder generally has no further contribution relating to those shares
The company continues despite the death or departure of a member
Company assets belong to the company rather than directly to shareholders
Ownership interests may pass between persons without terminating the company

questions.rationale: These situations distinguish the major legal characteristics arising from incorporation and the corporate form.

questions.question: Match each regulatory body with its primary role in the corporate and financial reporting environment described in the chapter.

matchPairs.right: Administers and enforces corporate law and monitors relevant financial reporting compliance
Applies listing requirements to companies seeking to remain listed on the securities market
Develops and formulates Australian accounting standards
Provides broad oversight and strategic direction for the standard setting process
Develops international financial reporting standards for global use

questions.rationale: The bodies perform distinct but interconnected roles involving corporate regulation, market listing, national standard setting oversight and international standard development.

questions.question: Match each reporting or entity classification with the description that most accurately applies to it.

matchPairs.right: Designed for users unable to demand individually tailored financial information
Prepared for particular information needs rather than the common needs addressed by general purpose reporting
Has users reasonably expected to depend on general purpose financial reports
Applies full recognition, measurement and disclosure requirements
Retains recognition and measurement requirements while allowing reduced disclosures

questions.rationale: The classifications distinguish the purpose of financial reports, the entities expected to prepare general purpose reports and the levels of disclosure within differential reporting.
